context_requirements: Expression of OXTR, AVPR1A or AVPR2 on the cell surface; the nine landmark cell lines are non-neuronal and largely lack functional OXTR/AVPR1A/AVPR2 signalling
An intact Gq/11-phospholipase C-calcium or Gs-cAMP signalling axis coupled to the receptor
A cell context in which the receptor drives an active transcriptional programme (e.g. neuronal differentiation, beta-cell function); none of the nine lines is such a context
falsifiers: Reproducible, dose-dependent changes in the 978 landmark genes at 6 h or 24 h in any of the nine lines after 10 micromolar antagonist that are absent with vehicle
A shared transcriptional signature across the nine lines that is reversed by oxytocin receptor agonists
Evidence of OXTR, AVPR1A or AVPR2 expression and coupling in these lines combined with antagonist-dependent gene expression changes

evidence.supports: Oxytocin receptor antagonist L-371,257 blocks oxytocin-stimulated neurite outgrowth and cytoskeletal gene expression in SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells, showing antagonist activity requires a neuronal, OXTR-expressing context
Oxytocin-induced calcium influx and SHANK1/SHANK3 expression in SH-SY5Y cells is blocked by the oxytocin receptor antagonist L-371,257
Oxytocin receptor antagonist L-371,257 reduces retinoic-acid/oxytocin-stimulated projection length in U-87MG glioblastoma cells, and OXTR knockdown reduces viability

Vasopressin receptor (AVPR1A/AVPR1B/AVPR2) signalling in pancreatic beta cells is only partially blocked by an oxytocin receptor antagonist, indicating limited OXTR dependence outside specific contexts

Oxytocin-stimulated insulin secretion from islets and beta cells is annulled by the oxytocin receptor antagonist atosiban, demonstrating antagonist efficacy only in oxytocin-responsive endocrine cells
